T: Backyard barbecue. Fire up the grill.
D: Three friends grow up in South Central Los Angeles, guided or lost depending on who's there for them.
P: Serve the mains when Doughboy's welcome-home barbecue gets going.
S: Crispy baked wings tossed in honey barbecue sauce with a splash of hot sauce

Wings dried overnight, baked at 220C for 45 minutes, tossed in a sticky barbecue, honey and hot sauce glaze. Leave 1kg chicken wings uncovered in the fridge overnight, then toss with garlic powder and salt. Bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm barbecue sauce with honey and a splash of hot sauce, toss the wings through and serve with plenty of napkins.
Eggs with mustard, sweet relish and hot sauce, dusted with smoked paprika
Eggs boiled 10 minutes, yolks whipped with mayo, mustard, sweet relish and hot sauce, piped back, paprika on top.
Corner store onion dip with ridged chips
slow-browned onions in sour cream and cream cheese, salted crinkle-cuts, from the corner store

Onions cooked slow until deep brown, folded through sour cream and cream cheese with chives and a dash of Worcestershire, served with ridged salted chips. Slice 3 brown onions thinly and cook in 30g butter and a splash of oil over low heat for 35 minutes, stirring, until deep brown. Cool completely. Beat 250g sour cream with 125g soft cream cheese, a dash of Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper. Fold in the onions and a handful of chopped chives. Chill for an hour and serve with ridged potato chips.
M: Foil-baked paprika pork ribs finished over coals, with crunchy cabbage slaw

Pork ribs rubbed with paprika, brown sugar, garlic and cayenne, wrapped and baked at 150C for 2.5 hours, glazed with barbecue sauce over hot coals. Rub 2kg pork ribs with smoked paprika, brown sugar, garlic powder, cayenne and salt. Wrap in foil and bake at 150C for 2.5 hours. Unwrap, brush with barbecue sauce and finish over hot coals until sticky. Serve with a crunchy cabbage coleslaw.
Furious's table fried chicken and greens
brined, floured and fried crisp, mac and cheese, ham hock collards, after the fishing trip

Chicken pieces brined in buttermilk, fried crisp in seasoned flour, served with baked mac and cheese and collard-style greens braised with smoked ham hock. Soak 1.5kg chicken pieces in 500ml buttermilk with salt and hot sauce overnight. Simmer a ham hock in 1L water for 1 hour, add 2 bunches shredded silverbeet and cook 20 minutes. Boil 300g macaroni, stir through 250g grated cheddar and 300ml milk and bake at 190C for 20 minutes. Dredge the chicken in 300g flour with paprika and garlic powder and fry at 165C for 12 to 14 minutes until 74C inside.
W: Spiced mashed sweet potato custard in a sweet pastry crust
Roasted sweet potato mashed with butter, brown sugar, eggs, evaporated milk and spices, baked in a blind-baked case at 170C for 50 minutes.
K: Cranberry, pineapple and lemonade punch served from a cooler, no alcohol
Red fruit punch of cranberry juice, pineapple juice and lemonade, poured over ice from a big cooler.

dishes.make_ahead: Dry the wings the day before

steps.text: Leave the wings uncovered in the fridge overnight.
Toss with garlic powder and salt.
Bake at 220C until crisp.
Warm the barbecue sauce with honey and hot sauce.
Toss the wings through the sauce and serve with plenty of napkins.
Heat the oven to 220C. Whisk the flour, water, garlic powder and salt to a thin batter.
Coat the cauliflower and bake on a lined tray until crisp, turning once.
Warm the barbecue sauce with honey and hot sauce.
Toss the cauliflower through the sauce and bake for 5 more minutes.
Serve with plenty of napkins.
Boil the eggs, then cool and peel.
Halve the eggs and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, mustard, relish and hot sauce until smooth.
Pipe back into the whites.
Chill, then dust with smoked paprika.

dishes.make_ahead: Rub and wrap the ribs up to 1 day ahead and keep chilled; make the coleslaw up to 4 hours ahead; bake, then finish on the coals on the night

steps.text: Rub the ribs with paprika, brown sugar, garlic powder, cayenne and salt.
Wrap the ribs in foil.
Bake at 150C until tender.
Shred the cabbage and carrot and toss with mayonnaise for a crunchy coleslaw.
Unwrap the ribs, brush with barbecue sauce and finish over hot coals until sticky.

veg.make_ahead: Rub and wrap the cauliflower up to 4 hours ahead and keep chilled; make the coleslaw up to 4 hours ahead; bake, then finish on the coals on the night

steps.text: Cut each cauliflower into 4 thick wedges through the stem. Brush with the olive oil and rub with the paprika, brown sugar, garlic powder, cayenne and salt.
Wrap the wedges in foil in two parcels.
Bake at 180C for 40 minutes until a knife slides into the stem easily.
Shred the cabbage and carrot and toss with mayonnaise for a crunchy coleslaw.
Unwrap the cauliflower, brush with barbecue sauce and finish over hot coals until sticky and charred.
Roast the sweet potatoes until soft.
Line a tin with the pastry and blind bake until pale golden.
Mash the sweet potato with butter, sugar, eggs, evaporated milk, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Pour into the case and bake at 170C until just set.
Cool before slicing.

dishes.make_ahead: Mix the cranberry and pineapple juice up to 1 day ahead and chill; add the ice and lemonade just before serving so it stays fizzy

steps.text: Fill a big drink cooler with ice.
Pour in the cranberry and pineapple juice and stir.
Top up with cold lemonade just before everyone arrives so it stays fizzy.
Set out cups and let people help themselves.

s.note: Crispy baked wings tossed in honey barbecue sauce with a splash of hot sauce
s.how: Leave 1kg chicken wings uncovered in the fridge overnight, then toss with garlic powder and salt. Bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm barbecue sauce with honey and a splash of hot sauce, toss the wings through and serve with plenty of napkins.

s.note: Eggs with mustard, sweet relish and hot sauce, dusted with smoked paprika
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, yellow mustard, a spoon of sweet relish and a dash of hot sauce until smooth. Pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika. Serve chilled on the porch.

m.note: Foil-baked paprika pork ribs finished over coals, with crunchy cabbage slaw
m.how: Rub 2kg pork ribs with smoked paprika, brown sugar, garlic powder, cayenne and salt. Wrap in foil and bake at 150C for 2.5 hours. Unwrap, brush with barbecue sauce and finish over hot coals until sticky. Serve with a crunchy cabbage coleslaw.

w.note: Spiced mashed sweet potato custard in a sweet pastry crust
w.how: Roast 800g sweet potatoes until soft, then mash with 60g butter, 150g brown sugar, 2 eggs, 200ml evaporated milk, cinnamon and nutmeg. Pour into a blind-baked sweet shortcrust case and bake at 170C for 50 minutes until just set. Cool before slicing.

d.note: Cranberry, pineapple and lemonade punch served from a cooler, no alcohol
d.how: Fill a big drink cooler with ice. Pour in 1L cranberry juice and 1L pineapple juice and stir. Top up with 2L cold lemonade just before everyone arrives so it stays fizzy. Set out plastic cups and let people help themselves all afternoon.
